newsitem.title: FRANCE: Chirac to make tv address, early French poll seen.
newsitem.headline: Chirac to make tv address, early French poll seen.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac will broadcast to the nation on Monday at 8 p.m. (1800 GMT), his office announced, amid expectations he will announce an early general election in late May or early June.

Chirac set the procedure for dissolving the National Assembly in motion by holding statutory consultations with Prime Minister Alain Juppe and the presidents of both houses of parliament on Monday morning.

Political sources said Chirac had decided to call a snap poll nine months ahead of schedule to clear the decks before France makes final efforts to ensure it qualifies for a single European currency due to begin in January 1999.

Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told Europe 1 radio on Monday there were economic advantages to bringing forward the election due next March, since investment decisions were being delayed because of political uncertainty.

A SOFRES institute opinion poll published by the daily Le Figaro on Monday suggested the ruling centre-right coalition, which controls 478 of the Assembly's 577 seats, would lose up to 150 seats but keep an overall majority.

Socialist opposition leader Lionel Jospin said an early poll would be an admission of defeat by the government and said he would oppose any further tightening of austerity to meet the criteria for European economic and monetary union.
